content.text: No change-of-control trigger or Vendor-side exit exists anywhere in the document. Fallback is fully met.

input.quote: 22.2 A Party may at any time, with the prior written consent of the Management Committee, assign, sell or transfer the whole of its rights and obligations under this Agreement. The Management Committee must not unreasonably withhold or delay its approval.
input.rationale: Paragraph 22 is fully symmetrical (it binds every APCN 2 Party, including us) and satisfies the fallback on its material terms: 22.3(a)-(d) let any Party, including Teleglobe USA, transfer the whole of its rights and obligations to a successor, Parent Company, Subsidiary or Affiliate without any consent; 22.6 requires only timely written notice to the other Parties; 22.1/22.2 make all other whole transfers subject to Management Committee consent that "must not unreasonably withhold or delay"; and 30 binds successors and permitted assigns. There is no change-of-control provision anywhere in the Agreement, so no counterparty termination or re-pricing right is triggered by a change of control of Teleglobe USA, and the walk-away scenarios are absent. Short of the preferred position we note only minor points that are not redlined: partial assignments to affiliates under 22.4 are permitted only once per Assignee and do not release the Assignor, territorial assignments under 22.5 carry ownership/cost conditions, and there is no bar on a counterparty assigning to our competitor. Given the multilateral consortium structure, these fall short of preferred wording only and do not fail fallback.
